questions.question_text:
The colours of cars are:
red, blue, white, red, blue, red, white, red.
Which set of frequencies is correct?

options.why: This misses the final red car.
This swaps the red and blue frequencies.
This counts only one of the two white cars.

questions.solution_text: Red occurs $4$ times, blue $2$ times and white $2$ times.

questions.question_text:
Students report how many pets they own:
$0,1,2,1,0,2,1,1,0$.
Which set of frequencies is correct?

options.why: This leaves out the three answers of zero pets.
This swaps the frequencies for one and two pets.
This misses the final answer of zero pets.

questions.solution_text: $0$ occurs $3$ times, $1$ occurs $4$ times and $2$ occurs $2$ times.

questions.question_text: What frequency is shown by the scooter tally $\cancel{||||}\;\cancel{||||}\;||||$?

options.why: This counts only the two complete groups of five and ignores four marks.
This counts one group of five and the final four, omitting another full group.
This treats the final group of four as if it were a complete group of five.

questions.question_text:
A frequency table of car colours has rows for red, blue, white, black and other.
Why is there an other row?

options.text: It groups car colours that do not have a named row.
It gives the total number of cars.
options.why: This confuses one category's frequency with the total frequency.

options.text: It records the red cars a second time.
options.why: This counts the same red cars in two categories.

options.text: It shows how many people are in each car.
options.why: This changes the recorded information from car colour to passenger count.

questions.solution_text: There are more car colours than the named rows, so other groups the remaining colours.

questions.question_text:
Arrivals are observed in this order: scooter, bicycle, walk, walk, scooter, walk, bicycle.
Which set of frequencies is correct?

options.why: Records the third arrival as a scooter, moving one walk into the scooter column.
Stops recording after the sixth arrival, so the final bicycle is never tallied.
Makes both slips at once: one walk logged as a scooter and the last bicycle missed.

questions.solution_text: Walk appears $3$ times, scooter $2$ times and bicycle $2$ times; $3+2+2=7$.

questions.question_text:
The travel-mode tallies are walk $\cancel{||||}\;\cancel{||||}\;\cancel{||||}\;||$, scooter $\cancel{||||}\;\cancel{||||}\;|$, bicycle $\cancel{||||}\;|||$, and other $||||$.
How many students were surveyed in total?

options.why: This counts each of the six crossed groups as four instead of five, giving $14+9+7+4=34$.
This leaves out the four students recorded in other, giving $17+11+8=36$.
This counts only the six complete groups of five and ignores all remaining marks.

questions.solution_text:
The frequencies are walk $17$, scooter $11$, bicycle $8$ and other $4$.
$17+11+8+4=40$ students.
